newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malay premier silent on 1999 party election plans.
newsitem.headline: Malay premier silent on 1999 party election plans.

text.p: Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad said on Saturday it was too early for him to say if he would stand for re-election as president of his political party in 1999.

"Why should we look so far ahead? It (the contest) is still far away. In the meantime, we want to concentrate on what we're supposed to do," he told a news conference at the end of the three-day annual general assembly of the United Malays National Organisation (UMNO).
By political convention, the president and deputy president of UMNO serve as prime minister and deputy prime minister.
Mahathir on Friday said he and UMNO's deputy president, Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim, were willing to contest their respective posts if the fight is clean.
UMNO is the main political party in the ruling National Front coalition, which has governed Malaysia since independence from Britain in 1957.
Mahathir and Anwar were not challenged in this year's triennial polls, viewed as more significant than a general election, which the National Front has always won easily.
Mahathir had banned all forms of campaigning by candidates in this year's elections and declared war on growing corruption in his political party.
Anwar told the news conference he was completely loyal to Mahathir, and that there was no "Mahathir camp or Anwar camp" as reported by the foreign media.

"Even though those personalities (who won the party polls on Wednesday and Thursday) are closely associated with me, I have total and complete loyalty to Dr Mahathir. Therefore, the press reports are irrelevant," Anwar said.
